judged_text: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar was set to null two lines above (neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists), silently discarding every collected team member calendar. For COLLECTIVE events where the organizer has no calendar connected but team members do, the members' destination calendars are dropped and events are created only from the organizer's credentials — the multi-host bug this PR claims to fix persists in that configuration.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [..] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [..] : null`. Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so the optional-chained `push` is a no-op and all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently dropped. This is verifiable from the diff and can prevent team members' calendars from being used in this configuration.
